newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish 1-day rates trough, zloty gains vs basket.
newsitem.headline: Polish 1-day rates trough, zloty gains vs basket.

text.p: Polish one-day deposit rates plunged in late trade after this morning's jump as players with money surpluses in the vital last days of the monthly reserve period cashed in on soaring rates, dealers said.

They said the shortage vanished near the end of the session after several players placed a total of 250 million zlotys on the market, aiding takers who lifted rates to around the 25 percent lombard rate in search of cash.
"Large lenders cashed in when prices approached the lombard rate," said one dealer at a Polish bank.
Overnight rates closed at 18.75/20.75 percent, down from intraday highs at 24.5 and this morning's 19.90/20.10 percent.
Tomorrow/next rates were at 19.50/21.50 percent, off highs at around 25 percent and yesterday's 19.30/19.55 percent.
Dealers said net flows with the clearing house could have played an important factor today and may decide whether Wednesday's swings in one-day rates would carry to Thursday.
They said clearing house flows were crucial ahead of Friday, the last working day of November's reserve period, which ends on Sunday, December 1.
"Sometimes banks need cash to square accounts at the morning's clearing session while the afternoon sessions gives them an unexpected inflow," said Anna Biernat from BRE SA.

Dealers said the money market's cash shortage also caused a run for the zloty on the forex market today, which lifted the Polish unit against the basket of currencies despite stable dollar/mark and the absence of market moving client orders.
The zloty firmed to 2.29/2.24 percent from the trading band centre from Tuesday's 2.13/2.08 percent as players shortened foreign currency positions to gain money market liquidity.
The zloty closed at 2.8320/30 to the dollar, up from 2.8385/95 on Tuesday and at 1.8580/90 per mark from 1.8583/93.
Dealers said the zloty may lose ground against the basket and shift back toward 2.10 percent from a trading band centre on Thursday as banks lenghten currency positions cut today.

"It is very likely that the zloty will lose ground tomorrow when the banks start lenghtening currency exposure cut on Wednesday to gain the zloty liquidity," said Marcin Stefaniuk from Bank Depozytowo-Kredytowy SA.
